svg.text: How to do APIs · The API Evangelist Transit Map

311 stops: the 30 lifecycle stages (★) and the policies that apply at each · 30 lines, one per stage, in six districts from Define to Deprecate · 62 strategies as express routes · click any stop for its strategies, experiences and rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Lifecycle stage", "name": "Domains", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/domains/", "text": "Every API begins with the domain it serves. Before I write a single line of a definition I get clear on the business domain, the bounded context, and who owns it, because the domain is what keeps an API coherent as it grows. Getting the domain right up front is what stops APIs from sprawling into overlapping, redundant messes down the road.", "groups": [["Phase", [{"name": "Define"}]], ["Policies at this stage", [{"name": "GitHub Organization README", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/github-organization-readme/"}, {"name": "GitHub Organization Repositories", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/github-organization-repositories/"}, {"name": "GitHub Organization Teams", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/github-organization-teams/"}, {"name": "GitHub Organizations", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/github-organization/"}, {"name": "Maintainers", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/maintainers/"}, {"name": "Teams", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/teams/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Lifecycle stage", "name": "Review", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/review/", "text": "Review is where a contract gets a second set of eyes before it leaves a stage \u2014 the paths, methods, status codes, and schema checked against the policy, in person or self-service. I have stopped treating the review as the place I make teams comply. The job is to conduct the review, surface the findings, and capture the provenance: the conversation happened, the decision got recorded, and whoever chose to defer owns that on the record with a reason attached.", "groups": [["Phase", [{"name": "Design"}]], ["Policies at this stage", []]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Lifecycle stage", "name": "Virtualization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/virtualization/", "text": "Before I build the real thing, I mock it. Virtualizing an API from its definition lets consumers and my own teams start integrating against a realistic contract while the backend is still being built. Mocking early surfaces design problems while they are still cheap to fix.", "groups": [["Phase", [{"name": "Design"}]], ["Policies at this stage", [{"name": "API Mocking (CI/CD)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/cicd-api-mocking/"}, {"name": "Sandbox (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-sandbox/"}]]]}
a.title: Virtualization — lifecycle stage (Design) Before I build the real thing, I mock it. Virtualizing an API from its definition lets consumers and my own teams start integrating against a realistic contract while the backend is still being built.

a.data-info: {"kind": "Lifecycle stage", "name": "Deployment", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deployment/", "text": "Deployment is how a definition becomes a running API. Whether it is a gateway, a serverless function, or a container, I want deployment to be automated, repeatable, and driven from the same contract everything else uses. Consistent deployment is what lets me ship APIs the same way every time instead of reinventing it per project.", "groups": [["Phase", [{"name": "Develop"}]], ["Policies at this stage", [{"name": "Deployment Is Automated", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/deployment-automated/"}, {"name": "Deployment Environments Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/deployment-environments/"}, {"name": "Gateways", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/gateway/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Agent Readiness with agents.md", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/agent-readiness-agents-md/", "text": "I require that every API provider ships an agents.md file that tells an automated consumer exactly how to behave when working with the API, including the conventions, the guardrails, and the workflows we expect agents to follow. This is the operating manual we would hand a capable junior engineer, except it is written for a machine that will read it literally. I insist on it because agents will act on our APIs with or without our guidance, and the responsible move is to author that guidance ourselves rather than let each integrator invent their own assumptions. Every API must treat agents.md as a first-class contract artifact, versioned and maintained alongside the code.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Ready for AI Agents", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-ready-for-ai-agents/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Agent Agents Md Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-agent-agents-md-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Agent Readiness with agents.md — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Agent Readiness with llms.txt", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/agent-readiness-llms-txt/", "text": "I require that every API publishes an llms.txt file at a predictable, well-known location so that large language models and the agents built on them can find a concise, curated map of what the API is and how to work with it. This file should point to the documentation, the OpenAPI, and the entry points that matter, written in plain language a model can actually parse. I care about this because agents are becoming first-class consumers, and if we leave them to guess by scraping marketing pages we get brittle, expensive, and wrong integrations. A small text file, maintained deliberately, is how we stay legible to the machines now reading our APIs.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Legible to Automated Consumers", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-legible-to-automated-consumers/"}, {"name": "APIs Are Ready for AI Agents", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-ready-for-ai-agents/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Agent LLMs Txt Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-agent-llms-txt-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Agent Readiness with llms.txt — policy 2 strategies · 5 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Agent-Scoped Authentication", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/agent-scoped-authentication/", "text": "I require that APIs support authentication credentials scoped specifically to agents, so that an autonomous consumer acts under its own narrowly-bound identity with least-privilege scopes rather than borrowing a human user's broad session. Every agent-facing API must let us issue, constrain, and revoke these credentials independently, and must make the intended scopes discoverable through the definition. I hold this line at design time because agents can act quickly and at scale, and a credential that was fine for a person becomes a real liability in the hands of software that never sleeps. Scoping authentication to the agent is how we keep automated access auditable, bounded, and safe to revoke without breaking everything else.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Authentication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/authentication/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Ready for AI Agents", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-ready-for-ai-agents/"}, {"name": "APIs Expose an MCP Server", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-expose-an-mcp-server/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}]]]}
a.title: Agent-Scoped Authentication — policy 2 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API Education and Enablement", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/api-education-and-enablement/", "text": "Require that an API invests in educating and enabling its consumers through tutorials, guides, and clear explanations of not just how it works but why. Most friction around APIs comes from gaps in understanding rather than technology, and raising API literacy pays off every time someone integrates faster or avoids a mistake. Enablement is a core responsibility of an API operation, not an afterthought bolted on at the end.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Educate and Enable Consumers", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-educate-and-enable-consumers/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Education", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/education/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: API Education and Enablement — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API Exit and Migration Path", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/api-exit-and-migration-path/", "text": "Require that an API documents a clear path for consumers to migrate onto, between, or off of it without being stranded. Lock-in by design erodes trust, so an honest operation makes leaving possible even as it works to earn consumers staying. A well-defined exit and migration path is what lets people commit to an API without fear of being trapped later.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Deprecation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deprecation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Avoid Vendor Lock-In", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-avoid-vendor-lock-in/"}, {"name": "APIs Support Data Portability and Ownership", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-data-portability-and-ownership/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Portability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/portability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Openness", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/openness/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API Outreach and Content", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/api-outreach-and-content/", "text": "Require that an API is actively communicated through ongoing content and outreach, including blog posts, changelogs, and updates that tell the story of what it does and why it matters. An API launched into silence will fail no matter how good it is, so sustained, honest communication is part of operating one responsibly. This is the work that turns a catalog of endpoints into something people actually discover and adopt.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Communication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Actively Evangelized", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-actively-evangelized/"}, {"name": "APIs Build and Nurture Community", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-build-and-nurture-community/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Advocacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/advocacy/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Community", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/community/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Arazzo Workflows Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/arazzo-workflows-provided/", "text": "Require that APIs which chain multiple operations to accomplish real work provide Arazzo workflow definitions describing those sequences. I want the multi-step paths a consumer must follow, the order, the inputs, and the outputs handed off between calls, expressed as machine-readable workflows rather than left to prose and tribal knowledge. Arazzo turns an integration from a puzzle into a followable, testable recipe, and it makes those recipes discoverable and reusable across teams and agents. I hold provided workflows as a design-time expectation for any API whose value depends on orchestrating several operations.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Provide Orchestration Workflows", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-provide-orchestration-workflows/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Arazzo Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-arazzo-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Arazzo Workflows Provided — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "AsyncAPI Contracts Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/asyncapi-contracts-provided/", "text": "I require that any event-driven or messaging interface is described with an AsyncAPI document, the same way we insist on OpenAPI for request-response APIs, so that channels, messages, and payloads are a governed contract rather than tribal knowledge. Every asynchronous API must define its channels and give its interface a proper title and version, because consumers of a message stream deserve the same legibility and tooling that HTTP consumers already take for granted. I care about this because the async side of our architecture is too often undocumented and discovered only by reading source code, which is exactly how integrations rot. AsyncAPI turns our event surface into something we can validate, publish, and reuse.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Definitions", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/definitions/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Use the Right Protocol for the Job", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-use-the-right-protocol-for-the-job/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "AsyncAPI Info Title Error", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/asyncapi-info-title-error/"}, {"name": "AsyncAPI Channels Defined Error", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/asyncapi-channels-defined-error/"}]]]}
a.title: AsyncAPI Contracts Provided — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 2 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Caching Strategy Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/caching-strategy-defined/", "text": "Every API should define a caching strategy and express it through explicit Cache-Control headers on responses that can safely be reused. I require that providers decide, per operation, what is cacheable, for how long, and by whom, rather than leaving consumers and gateways to guess. A deliberate caching strategy cuts latency, reduces load, and lowers cost for both sides of the contract. Silent or absent caching directives waste compute and produce inconsistent behavior across clients, so I hold a documented caching posture as a performance baseline.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Caching", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/caching/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Fast and Efficient", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-fast-and-efficient/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "OpenAPI Response Cache Control Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-response-cache-control-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Caching Strategy Defined — policy 1 strategies · 2 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API Mocking (CI/CD)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/cicd-api-mocking/", "text": "Require that every API can be mocked directly from its contract so consumers and downstream teams can build against it before the implementation is finished. I lean on mocking because it is what makes design-first real, letting the frontend, the integrator, and the test suite start work off the OpenAPI the moment it stabilizes. Stand the mock up in CI/CD from the same contract that will govern production, and you turn the specification into a working, testable thing instead of a document. This is how you parallelize delivery and catch design problems while they are still cheap to fix.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Virtualization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/virtualization/"}, {"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}, {"name": "API Governance Is Automated in CI/CD", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-governance-is-automated-in-cicd/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: API Mocking (CI/CD) — policy 2 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Contract Testing (CI/CD)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/cicd-contract-testing/", "text": "Require that every API is tested against its own contract in the CI/CD pipeline so the running service can never quietly drift from the OpenAPI it publishes. I insist on contract testing because a spec that lies is worse than no spec at all, and the only way to keep the two honest is to check them on every build. Validate requests, responses, status codes, and schemas against the contract, and fail the pipeline when they diverge. This is the automated conscience that lets teams move fast while keeping the promise their documentation makes to consumers.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Definitions", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/definitions/"}, {"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}, {"name": "API Governance Is Automated in CI/CD", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-governance-is-automated-in-cicd/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Contract Testing (CI/CD) — policy 2 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Linting (CI/CD)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/cicd-linting/", "text": "Require that every API contract is automatically linted against our design and governance rules on each commit, so standards are enforced by machines rather than by memory and goodwill. I love linting because it moves governance to the left, catching naming, structure, security, and documentation problems in seconds while the author still has context. Wire a ruleset like Spectral into CI/CD and make it a gate, and consistency stops being a style debate and becomes a build result. This is the single highest-leverage way I know to scale good API design across a lot of teams.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}, {"name": "API Governance Is Automated in CI/CD", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-governance-is-automated-in-cicd/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Linting (CI/CD) — policy 2 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Schema Registry (CI/CD)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/cicd-schema-registry/", "text": "Require that the schemas an API relies on are published to a shared schema registry and validated against it in CI/CD, so the shapes of our data are versioned, discoverable, and compatible. I want a registry because the same data structures show up across many APIs and events, and letting each team redefine them privately is how drift and duplication creep in. Register the schemas, check compatibility on every change, and reuse them by reference instead of copy and paste. This gives us one source of truth for our data contracts and turns compatibility from a hope into a checked guarantee.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}, {"name": "API Governance Is Automated in CI/CD", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-governance-is-automated-in-cicd/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Schema Registry (CI/CD) — policy 2 strategies · 10 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Communication Status Page", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/communication-status-page/", "text": "Every API must maintain a public status page that reports current health, active incidents, and scheduled maintenance in real time. I require that consumers be able to check the state of an API themselves rather than filing a ticket to learn whether the provider already knows about an outage. A status page is how a provider communicates honestly during the moments that matter most, and it is the difference between transparency and silence when things go wrong. I hold a discoverable, well-maintained status page as a production-grade requirement for building trust.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Communication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Monitoring", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monitoring/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable Across Operations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-across-operations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}]]]}
a.title: Communication Status Page — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Community Engagement Channels", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/community-engagement-channels/", "text": "Require that an API provides real channels for its community to engage, whether a forum, chat, mailing list, or regular office hours. Consumers need a place to ask questions, share solutions, and connect with the provider and each other, and the operation needs that signal to improve. A living community becomes a source of support and feedback no internal team could replicate on its own.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Communication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Build and Nurture Community", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-build-and-nurture-community/"}, {"name": "APIs Invest in Developer Relations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-invest-in-developer-relations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Community", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/community/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Advocacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/advocacy/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Community Engagement Channels — policy 2 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Consent and DPA Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/consent-and-dpa-provided/", "text": "Every API that touches personal data must provide a data processing agreement and a clear record of the consent under which that data is handled. I require that the DPA be available to consumers before they integrate, and that consent records establish who agreed to what and when. This is not paperwork for its own sake; it is the legal spine that lets consumers build on an API without inheriting unbounded compliance risk. Providers who make the DPA and consent posture explicit earn trust and shorten every procurement conversation that follows.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Terms of Service", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/terms-of-service/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Transparent and Accountable", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-transparent-and-accountable/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}]]]}
a.title: Consent and DPA Provided — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Consumer Rights Honored", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/consumer-rights-honored/", "text": "Require that an API honors the rights of its consumers and the people its data represents, including access, correction, portability, and deletion. As APIs become the infrastructure of public and economic life, the operations behind them carry real responsibility for how that power is used. Honoring consumer rights transparently builds the kind of durable trust that regulation and backlash cannot easily shake.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Serve the Public Interest", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-serve-the-public-interest/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Openness", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/openness/"}]]]}
a.title: Consumer Rights Honored — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Ownership Respected", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/data-ownership-respected/", "text": "Require that an API respects the ownership of the data it handles, treating consumer and end-user data as belonging to them rather than to whoever stores it. Ownership shapes what a provider may do with data, how consent is honored, and how portability and deletion are handled. Being explicit about data ownership is foundational to the trust consumers place in an API and to meeting rising regulatory expectations.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Support Data Portability and Ownership", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-data-portability-and-ownership/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Portability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/portability/"}]]]}
