a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Portability Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/data-portability-provided/", "text": "Require that consumers can export their data from an API in a portable, standard format without friction or penalty. The data flowing through an API belongs to the people and organizations it describes, and they should be able to take it elsewhere whenever they choose. Providing real portability is a statement of confidence, and paradoxically the providers most willing to let consumers leave are the ones consumers most want to stay with.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Serve the Public Interest", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-serve-the-public-interest/"}, {"name": "APIs Support Data Portability and Ownership", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-data-portability-and-ownership/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Portability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/portability/"}, {"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Openness", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/openness/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Portability Provided — policy 2 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Privacy and PII Classified", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/data-privacy-pii-classified/", "text": "I require that every schema property carrying personally identifiable information is explicitly classified as such in the API definition, so that PII is visible to governance, tooling, and downstream consumers rather than hidden inside an ordinary-looking field. Classifying PII at design time is how we make privacy enforceable instead of aspirational, because you cannot protect, redact, or account for data you have not first identified. I insist on this because privacy obligations follow the data wherever it flows, and an unlabeled PII field is a compliance incident waiting to be discovered by someone other than us. Every API that touches personal data must classify it in the contract.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Respect Data Privacy and Residency", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-respect-data-privacy-and-residency/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "OpenAPI Schema Property PII Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-schema-property-pii-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Privacy and PII Classified — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Residency Enforced", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/data-residency-enforced/", "text": "I require that every API declares where the data it handles is stored and processed, and that those residency commitments are actually enforced rather than merely stated in a policy document. Consumers in regulated markets need to know their data stays within a given jurisdiction, and that guarantee only means something if the platform enforces it and can prove it. I hold this as a production governance requirement because data residency is increasingly a legal precondition for doing business at all, and a violation is not a bug you patch quietly but a breach of trust and law. Every API must make its residency commitments explicit and keep them honest.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Respect Data Privacy and Residency", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-respect-data-privacy-and-residency/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Residency Enforced — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Retention Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/data-retention-defined/", "text": "Require that every API declare a written retention policy stating how long each category of data is kept, why it is kept, and when it is destroyed. I expect this policy to be discoverable alongside the API, not buried in a contract only lawyers ever read. Retention rules protect consumers, satisfy regulators, and keep providers honest about the data they hold. Undefined retention is a liability that grows quietly until it becomes a breach or an audit finding, so I treat a documented RetentionPolicy as a baseline requirement for any production API.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Transparent and Accountable", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-transparent-and-accountable/"}, {"name": "APIs Respect Data Privacy and Residency", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-respect-data-privacy-and-residency/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Privacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/privacy/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Retention Defined — policy 2 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Dependency SBOM Maintained", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/dependency-sbom-maintained/", "text": "Require that every API maintain a current software bill of materials enumerating the libraries, services, and versions it depends on. I want a machine-readable SBOM and dependency manifest kept in sync with what actually ships, so we can answer what is inside an API the moment a vulnerability is disclosed. You cannot secure or evaluate a dependency you have not inventoried, and an out-of-date SBOM is worse than none because it lies about exposure. I hold a maintained SBOM as a production requirement for provenance, security response, and honest procurement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Dependencies Have an SBOM", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-dependencies-have-an-sbom/"}, {"name": "APIs Are Evaluated Before Adoption", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-evaluated-before-adoption/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Procurement", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/procurement/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Reuse", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reuse/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Dependency SBOM Maintained — policy 2 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Deployment Is Automated", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/deployment-automated/", "text": "Require that every API be deployed through an automated, repeatable pipeline rather than by hand. I want the path from a merged change to a running endpoint to be codified, versioned, and reproducible on demand. Manual deployments drift, hide tribal knowledge, and turn routine releases into risky events. Automating deployment gives us consistent environments, faster recovery, and a clear audit trail for how each API reached production, which is why I hold it as a baseline expectation for teams shipping APIs.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Deployment", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deployment/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Deployed Consistently and Automatically", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-deployed-consistently/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}]]]}
a.title: Deployment Is Automated — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Deployment Environments Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/deployment-environments/", "text": "Every API must define its deployment environments explicitly, naming where it runs across development, staging, and production and how consumers reach each one. I require that base URLs, credentials, and behavior differences between environments be documented so no one guesses which endpoint they are hitting. Clear environment definitions let consumers test safely before they commit to production and let providers promote changes with confidence. Ambiguity about environments is a common source of outages and leaked test data, so I treat an explicit Environments declaration as a requirement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Deployment", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deployment/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Deployed Consistently and Automatically", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-deployed-consistently/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}]]]}
a.title: Deployment Environments Defined — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Deprecation Sunset Headers", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/deprecation-sunset-headers/", "text": "Every deprecated API operation must announce itself in-band using Deprecation and Sunset headers that tell consumers a change is coming and when it lands. I require that deprecation be signaled through the response itself, not only in a changelog a consumer may never read. Machine-readable sunset dates let clients and agents plan migrations before an endpoint disappears, which is the difference between an orderly transition and a broken integration. I treat clear deprecation signaling as a baseline courtesy and a governance requirement for any API that changes over time.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Deprecation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deprecation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable Across Operations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-across-operations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "OpenAPI Operation Deprecated Sunset Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-deprecated-sunset-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Deprecation Sunset Headers — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API First (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-api-first/", "text": "Require that every API begins with a design-first contract, an OpenAPI definition authored and agreed upon before a single line of implementation code is written. I have watched too many teams code an API into existence and then reverse-engineer a spec to match, and it always shows in the seams. When we lead with the contract, product, engineering, and consumers can all react to the same source of truth early, mock against it, and catch expensive design mistakes while they are still cheap to fix. This is the discipline that makes fast, predictable delivery possible instead of a hopeful accident.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: API First (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Async Webhooks (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-async-webhooks/", "text": "Require that any API delivering events to consumers describes its webhooks as first-class citizens in the contract, using the OpenAPI webhooks object to define the payloads, headers, and callbacks a subscriber should expect. I have chased too many undocumented webhooks that only lived in a provider's head or a support thread, and that opacity erodes trust fast. When we treat outbound events with the same rigor as inbound requests, consumers can build resilient, event-driven integrations without guessing, and we can version and evolve those events responsibly. Async is not an excuse to skip the contract, it is a reason to be more explicit about it.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Support Event-Driven and Asynchronous Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-event-driven-and-asynchronous-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Async Webhooks (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Batch Operations (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-batch-operations/", "text": "Require that APIs handling high volumes of records offer explicit batch operations rather than forcing consumers to hammer single-resource endpoints in a loop. Every API must define clear semantics for how a batch request is submitted, how partial success and per-item errors are reported, and what limits apply. I have seen well-meaning integrations melt a backend simply because the only path forward was thousands of individual calls, and that is a design failure, not a consumer failure. Thoughtful batch endpoints let both sides scale efficiently and keep the contract honest about what the platform can actually sustain under load.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Scale Efficiently Under Load", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-scale-efficiently-under-load/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Batch Operations (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Best Practices (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-best-practices/", "text": "Require that every API adheres to the shared design best practices we have codified across the platform, so that consistency is a default and not something each team reinvents. Every API must reflect the accumulated, boring, hard-won wisdom of how our APIs behave, from resource modeling to response shapes to error conventions. I am not interested in clever, one-off designs that surprise consumers, I want APIs that feel familiar the moment a developer opens them. When best practices are written down and enforced through governance, we turn tribal knowledge into something teachable, reviewable, and durable across the whole API estate.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}
a.title: Best Practices (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Compatibility (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-compatibility/", "text": "Require that changes to an API preserve backward compatibility by default, and that any deviation is a deliberate, governed decision rather than an accident of a merge. Every API must be designed so new fields, optional parameters, and additive changes never break existing consumers, and so the contract evolves without pulling the rug out from under people. I have felt the pain on both sides of a surprise breaking change, and it is one of the fastest ways to lose the trust you spent years earning. Designing for compatibility also keeps our APIs interoperable across systems, where a small incautious change can ripple far beyond the team that made it.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Versioning", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/versioning/"}, {"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Interoperable Across Systems", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-interoperable-across-systems/"}, {"name": "Breaking Changes Are Prevented or Carefully Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/breaking-changes-are-prevented-or-carefully-managed/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Compatibility (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 12 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Types (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-data-types/", "text": "Require that every property in an API contract declares an explicit, well-chosen data type with the right format, precision, and constraints instead of leaning on loose strings and hopeful parsing. Every API must be precise about whether a value is an integer, a date-time, a decimal, an enum, or something else, because that precision is what makes the data trustworthy on the other end. I have debugged too many integrations that broke on an ambiguous number or a date that everyone interpreted differently. Getting data types right up front is how we make APIs interoperable, consistent, and safe to validate automatically across every consumer that touches them.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Interoperable Across Systems", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-interoperable-across-systems/"}, {"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}, {"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Types (Design) — policy 3 strategies · 13 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Hypermedia (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-hypermedia/", "text": "Require that APIs return links alongside their data where it helps consumers navigate related resources, discover available actions, and follow state transitions without hardcoding URLs. APIs should treat hypermedia as a first-class design tool, using consistent link relations so that a client can move through the API by following links rather than by assembling paths from documentation and guesswork. I know hypermedia can be overdone, so I am not asking for dogma, I am asking for links where they reduce coupling and make integrations more resilient. When responses carry their own navigation, our APIs stay interoperable and clients survive change far more gracefully.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Interoperable Across Systems", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-interoperable-across-systems/"}, {"name": "APIs Support Event-Driven and Asynchronous Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-event-driven-and-asynchronous-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Hypermedia (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Idempotency (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-idempotency/", "text": "Require that state-changing operations be safe to retry, either because the method is inherently idempotent or because the API supports an idempotency key that lets a consumer replay a request without creating duplicate side effects. Every API must assume that networks fail, timeouts happen, and clients will retry, so a double-submitted payment or a duplicated order is a design problem we own, not the consumer's fault. I have watched real money and real trust get lost to retries that quietly did the same thing twice. Building idempotency into the contract is what makes event-driven and asynchronous patterns dependable instead of a source of quiet corruption.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}, {"name": "APIs Support Event-Driven and Asynchronous Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-event-driven-and-asynchronous-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}
a.title: Idempotency (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Long Running Operations (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-long-running-operations/", "text": "Require that operations which cannot complete within a normal request window be modeled explicitly as asynchronous, long-running jobs rather than being forced into a single blocking call that ties up connections and times out. Every API with heavy work must accept the request, return a job or operation resource the consumer can poll or subscribe to, and expose clear status, progress, and result semantics. I have seen far too many APIs try to do minutes of work inside one HTTP call and then blame the client for the timeout. Designing long-running operations properly is how we keep the platform responsive and let consumers build reliable, event-driven workflows on top of it.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Support Event-Driven and Asynchronous Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-support-event-driven-and-asynchronous-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Long Running Operations (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Media Types (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-media-types/", "text": "Require that every request and response declares an accurate, standard media type, and that content negotiation is handled deliberately rather than assumed to always be JSON. Every API must be explicit about the formats it accepts and produces, use registered media types, and reserve vendor-specific types for cases that genuinely need them. I have hit too many endpoints that lied about their content type or silently ignored the Accept header, and that ambiguity breaks tooling and interoperability. Getting media types right is a small, unglamorous discipline that keeps our APIs consistent and lets clients across many languages and platforms integrate without surprises.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Interoperable Across Systems", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-interoperable-across-systems/"}, {"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}
a.title: Media Types (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Naming Conventions (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-naming-conventions/", "text": "Require that every API follows a single, documented set of naming conventions for resources, fields, parameters, and enums, so a developer who learns one of our APIs already understands the next. Every API must be consistent about casing, pluralization, and vocabulary, because these small choices are the texture a consumer feels on every call. I care about this more than it may seem, since inconsistent naming is one of the loudest signals that an organization has no real governance behind its APIs. When names are predictable, the whole platform reads like it was built by one thoughtful team, and that consistency compounds into a genuinely better developer experience.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Standardization", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/standardization/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}
a.title: Naming Conventions (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Robustness (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-robustness/", "text": "Require that APIs are designed for robustness on both sides of the wire, being conservative in what they send and tolerant in what they accept, so that small variations do not cascade into outages. Every API must ignore unknown fields gracefully, avoid brittle assumptions about ordering or optional data, and be built to survive the messy reality of real-world clients. I lean on the robustness principle because it is what lets an API evolve without breaking the integrations built on top of it. Designing for tolerance is how we keep APIs interoperable across systems and how we manage change without punishing consumers for being slightly out of step.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Interoperable Across Systems", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-interoperable-across-systems/"}, {"name": "Breaking Changes Are Prevented or Carefully Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/breaking-changes-are-prevented-or-carefully-managed/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Robustness (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 12 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "URL Structure (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-url-structure/", "text": "Require that every API uses a consistent, predictable URL structure, with clear resource hierarchies, sensible pluralization, and paths that read like the nouns of the domain rather than a grab bag of verbs. Every API must model its paths the same way, so consumers can often guess the next endpoint before they even open the docs. I have learned that URL design is the first impression an API makes, and messy, inconsistent paths signal a lack of care that undermines everything else. When our URLs follow shared conventions, the platform feels coherent, tooling works better, and developers spend their energy on their integration instead of decoding our routing choices.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}
a.title: URL Structure (Design) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Validation (Design)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/design-validation/", "text": "Require that every API defines and enforces validation rules in its contract, using schemas, constraints, required fields, and formats so that bad input is rejected with a clear, consistent error instead of silently corrupting data downstream. Every API must make its expectations explicit and machine-readable, so validation can be generated, tested, and enforced automatically rather than reimplemented by hand in every service. I have cleaned up too many messes that started as an unvalidated field quietly accepted at the edge. Designing validation into the contract is how we keep our APIs consistent, catch problems early, and give consumers honest, actionable feedback.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}, {"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}]]]}
a.title: Validation (Design) — policy 2 strategies · 14 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Developer Relations Program", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/developer-relations-program/", "text": "Require that any API meant for real adoption is backed by a developer relations function responsible for supporting, advocating for, and growing its community of consumers. Endpoints and documentation are not enough; someone has to carry consumer feedback back into the operation and champion the developer's experience internally. I have watched developer relations quietly decide whether API programs succeed, because it is the human function that catches everything the tooling misses.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Communication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Actively Evangelized", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-actively-evangelized/"}, {"name": "APIs Invest in Developer Relations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-invest-in-developer-relations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Advocacy", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/advocacy/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Community", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/community/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Developer Relations Program — policy 2 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "DNS Is Managed", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/dns-managed/", "text": "Require that the DNS behind every API be deliberately managed, with ownership, records, and TTLs tracked as part of the API's operational contract. I expect hostnames to be stable, certificates to align with those hostnames, and changes to flow through a controlled process rather than an untracked console. DNS is the front door to an API, and when it is neglected it becomes the single point of failure that takes everything down. Treating DNS as a managed asset gives consumers reliable resolution and gives providers a clean way to move traffic without breaking integrations.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "DNS", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/dns/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Deployed Consistently and Automatically", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-deployed-consistently/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}]]]}
a.title: DNS Is Managed — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Documentation", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/", "text": "The human-readable HTML, Markdown, or PDF representation of the technical surface area of each API, providing path, methods, summaries, description, examples, and the other resources consumers will need.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Always Well Documented", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-always-well-documented/"}, {"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Apis Properties Documentation Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-apis-properties-documentation-info/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Documentation Paths", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/documentation-paths/", "text": "Providing simple, clean, and intuitive paths as part of the documentation being published for consumers to use.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Documentation Request Bodies", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/documentation-request-bodies/", "text": "Including details and examples regarding the request bodies being submitted for POST, PUT, and other possible methods.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Documentation Responses", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/documentation-responses/", "text": "Making sure there is a complete example for each API response in documentation, including happy and unhappy responses.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Environments", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/environments/", "text": "The environments for development, staging, or production environments should be available to manually or automatically working with an API in any environment, providing a machine-readable way for navigating each of the environments available for an API.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Made Available Through a Platform Gateway", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-made-available-through-a-platform-gateway/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Apis Properties Environments Production Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-apis-properties-environments-production-info/"}, {"name": "APIs.json Apis Properties Environments Staging Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-apis-properties-environments-staging-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Environments — policy 1 strategies · 10 experiences · 2 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Event Types Cataloged", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/event-types-cataloged/", "text": "I require that every event an API emits is enumerated in a published catalog of event types, each with a stable name, a described payload, and a clear meaning, so consumers know exactly what can happen and can subscribe to it deliberately. Events that only exist implicitly in the code are impossible to discover, impossible to govern, and impossible to reuse across teams. I push for this at design time and make it discoverable because the value of an event-driven system is only realized when the events themselves are a first-class, browsable part of the contract. Every API that produces events must maintain its event type catalog as a living artifact, not an afterthought.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Use the Right Protocol for the Job", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-use-the-right-protocol-for-the-job/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}
a.title: Event Types Cataloged — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "API Catalog (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-api-catalog/", "text": "Require that every API is registered in a central, searchable catalog with enough metadata that a developer can find it, understand it, and decide to use it without asking anyone. I care deeply about this because an API nobody can discover might as well not exist, and the biggest source of waste I see is teams rebuilding capabilities that already ship down the hall. The catalog should carry the name, description, owner, status, and links to docs and the contract, and it should be kept current as a condition of shipping. A good catalog is where reuse, self-service, and real API-as-a-product culture begin.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Discoverable Through a Central Catalog", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-discoverable-through-a-central-catalog/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Reuse", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reuse/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}]]]}
a.title: API Catalog (Experience) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Interactive Documentation (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-interactive-documentation/", "text": "Require that every API ships interactive documentation generated from its contract, where a developer can read the operations, see the schemas, and make a real call right from the page. I have believed for years that documentation is the interface to your API, and static reference pages that nobody trusts are a quiet tax on every integration. Drive the docs from the OpenAPI so they stay in sync, let people authenticate and try requests inline, and you shorten the distance between curiosity and a working call. This is one of the clearest investments a provider can make in developer experience.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}
a.title: Interactive Documentation (Experience) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Localization (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-localization/", "text": "Require that APIs serving a global audience localize the things developers and end users actually experience, from documentation and portal content to error messages, currencies, and date and time formats. I raise this because we too easily assume everyone reads English and lives in our timezone, and that assumption quietly excludes a lot of the world from building on our APIs. Decide deliberately which languages and locales you support, respect standards like Accept-Language and ISO codes, and be honest about it in the docs. Thoughtful localization is how an API becomes usable well beyond the market it was first designed for.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Migration Guides (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-migration-guides/", "text": "Require that whenever an API version is deprecated or a breaking change is introduced, a clear migration guide is published that shows consumers exactly how to move from the old to the new. I insist on this because a deprecation notice without a migration path is just an ultimatum, and it puts all the burden on the people who trusted us. A good guide spells out what changed, maps old fields and endpoints to new ones, and includes real examples so a developer can make the switch without reverse-engineering the diff. Writing these well is one of the most concrete ways a provider shows respect for the businesses built on its API.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Versioning Follows a Defined Standard", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-versioning-follows-a-defined-standard/"}, {"name": "APIs Are Gracefully Deprecated and Retired", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-gracefully-deprecated-and-retired/"}, {"name": "Breaking Changes Are Prevented or Carefully Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/breaking-changes-are-prevented-or-carefully-managed/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Migration Guides (Experience) — policy 3 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Sandbox (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-sandbox/", "text": "Require that every API offers a sandbox environment with test credentials and safe, representative data so a developer can experiment fully before touching production. I champion sandboxes because the fastest way to earn a developer's trust is to let them get a real response in minutes without risk, paperwork, or fear of breaking something. The sandbox should mirror the production contract, reset predictably, and be reachable straight from the portal and the docs. When people can play without consequences, they onboard faster, integrate more deeply, and arrive in production already confident.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Virtualization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/virtualization/"}, {"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Delivery Is Fast and Design-First", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-delivery-is-fast-and-design-first/"}, {"name": "APIs Deliver an Exceptional Developer Experience", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-deliver-an-exceptional-developer-experience/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Velocity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/velocity/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "SLA (Experience)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/experience-sla/", "text": "Require that every API published for consumers carries a clear service level agreement stating its uptime target, expected performance, support commitments, and what happens when we fall short. I push for explicit SLAs because a promise you will not write down is a promise you do not really mean, and consumers cannot build a serious business on vague assurances. Publish the numbers in the portal, back them with real monitoring and a status page, and be honest when the tier is best-effort. A well-defined SLA is where an API stops being a hobby and becomes something people can depend on.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Portal", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/portal/"}, {"name": "Terms of Service", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/terms-of-service/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Earn and Maintain Consumer Trust", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-earn-and-maintain-consumer-trust/"}, {"name": "APIs Have Clear Service Level Commitments", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-clear-service-level-commitments/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "FinOps Cost Visibility", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/finops-cost-visibility/", "text": "I require that the full cost of running an API is made visible through FinOps practices, so the people making decisions about an API can see what it actually costs to operate, not just what it earns. Every API in production should surface its cost signals alongside its usage and revenue, because a program that only measures adoption and ignores spend is flying blind toward an unpleasant surprise. I hold this position because sustainability is a governance concern, and an API we cannot afford to run is not a reliable API no matter how popular it becomes. FinOps visibility is how we keep the economics of our APIs honest and the whole portfolio sustainable over time.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Analytics", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/analytics/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Have a Sustainable Cost Model", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-a-sustainable-cost-model/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Sustainability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/sustainability/"}, {"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Compliance Mapping (Governance)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/governance-compliance-mapping/", "text": "Require that every API in production maps its endpoints, data, and controls to the specific regulatory and compliance obligations it falls under, whether that is GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2, or an internal policy. I have watched too many teams treat compliance as a spreadsheet someone fills out once a year, so I want the mapping to live alongside the API contract where it can be checked and audited. When we know which regulation touches which operation, we can prove coverage, spot the gaps before an auditor does, and stop guessing about who is exposed. This turns compliance from a fire drill into a property of the API itself.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Meet Regulatory and Compliance Requirements", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-meet-regulatory-and-compliance-requirements/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}]]]}
a.title: Compliance Mapping (Governance) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Dependency Management (Governance)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/governance-dependency-management/", "text": "Require that every API declares the upstream services, libraries, and other APIs it depends on, and keeps that list current as part of its governance record. I care about this because APIs never stand alone, and a change three hops away can quietly break something we own without anyone connecting the dots. When dependencies are tracked, we can reason about blast radius, plan migrations, and answer the question \"what breaks if this goes away\" before it becomes an incident. I would rather map these relationships on purpose than rediscover them at two in the morning.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Dependencies Are Tracked and Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-dependencies-are-tracked-and-managed/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}]]]}
a.title: Dependency Management (Governance) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Maturity Scoring (Governance)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/governance-maturity-scoring/", "text": "Require that every API is scored against a shared maturity model that measures design, documentation, testing, security, and operational readiness, and that the score is visible to the team that owns it. I like maturity scoring because it replaces opinion and politics with a number everyone can see and move, giving us a fair way to compare APIs and to celebrate real progress. The point is not to shame anyone, it is to make the next improvement obvious and to help leadership invest where the gaps actually are. When teams can watch their score climb, quality stops being abstract and becomes something they own.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Maturity Is Measured and Improved", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-maturity-is-measured-and-improved/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Policy Exceptions (Governance)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/governance-policy-exceptions/", "text": "Require that any deviation from a governance policy is requested, justified, time-boxed, and approved through a documented exception process rather than quietly ignored. I have learned that rigid rules with no escape hatch just get worked around in the dark, so I want a front door for exceptions that keeps them visible, owned, and expiring. Every exception should name who approved it, why it was granted, and when it must be revisited, so we can meet real deadlines without pretending our standards do not exist. This keeps governance honest and keeps our compliance posture defensible when someone asks how a rule got bent.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Meet Regulatory and Compliance Requirements", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-meet-regulatory-and-compliance-requirements/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}]]]}
a.title: Policy Exceptions (Governance) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Review & Approval (Governance)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/governance-review-approval/", "text": "Require that every API design and significant change passes through a documented review and approval step before it ships, with clear owners and clear criteria. I am a big believer in design-first review because the cheapest place to catch a bad decision is in the contract, long before code and consumers are built on top of it. A good review is collaborative, not a gate for its own sake, pulling in design, security, and the teams who will consume the API so problems surface early. When approval is explicit and recorded, we get accountability and a shared bar for quality instead of APIs slipping into production on nobody's watch.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Development Is Collaborative Across Teams", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-development-is-collaborative-across-teams/"}, {"name": "API Maturity Is Measured and Improved", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-maturity-is-measured-and-improved/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Workspaces", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/workspaces/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "GraphQL Schema Governed", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/graphql-schema-governed/", "text": "I require that any GraphQL API ships a published, versioned schema that we govern like any other contract, with consistent naming, deliberate types, and a clear boundary on what the graph exposes. A GraphQL endpoint without a governed schema is just a query surface that drifts, and consumers end up depending on fields we never meant to guarantee. I insist on this at design time because GraphQL gives consumers enormous flexibility, and that flexibility only stays safe when the schema behind it is held to a standard rather than accreted feature by feature. Every GraphQL API should treat its schema as the contract, reviewed and maintained with the same care we give an OpenAPI.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Use the Right Protocol for the Job", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-use-the-right-protocol-for-the-job/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Breaking Changes (Lifecycle)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/lifecycle-breaking-changes/", "text": "Require that breaking changes to a production API are identified, avoided where possible, and never shipped silently onto an existing version. I hold this line hard because a breaking change you did not announce is a betrayal of every consumer who trusted your contract, and trust is the whole point of doing APIs. When a breaking change is truly necessary, it should be delivered through a new version with a clear migration path and a deprecation window, not by mutating the endpoint people already depend on. Detecting these against the API contract in your pipeline is how you keep good intentions from turning into a 3 a.m. outage for somebody else.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Versioning", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/versioning/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Dependencies Are Tracked and Managed", "url":
