a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Change Management (Lifecycle)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/lifecycle-change-management/", "text": "Require that every change to a production API moves through a defined change management process that assesses impact, tracks dependencies, and communicates what is changing before it lands. I want change to be boring and predictable, because surprise is what erodes consumer confidence and turns small edits into incidents. That means knowing who depends on an operation, classifying whether a change is additive or breaking, and giving people notice and a changelog they can actually read. Managing change on purpose is how we keep moving fast without leaving our consumers behind.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Versioning", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/versioning/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Dependencies Are Tracked and Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-dependencies-are-tracked-and-managed/"}, {"name": "Breaking Changes Are Prevented or Carefully Managed", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/breaking-changes-are-prevented-or-carefully-managed/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]]]}
a.title: Change Management (Lifecycle) — policy 2 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Deprecation (Lifecycle)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/lifecycle-deprecation/", "text": "Require that any API or operation being retired is formally deprecated first, marked in the contract, and announced with a clear sunset date and migration guidance. I treat deprecation as a promise, not a surprise, because consumers built real businesses on your endpoints and they deserve a runway to move. Use the Deprecation and Sunset headers, flag it in the OpenAPI, and tell people in the changelog and in the portal so nobody finds out by getting an error. Graceful deprecation is one of the clearest signals that an API provider can be trusted over the long haul.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Versioning", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/versioning/"}, {"name": "Deprecation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deprecation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Gracefully Deprecated and Retired", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-gracefully-deprecated-and-retired/"}, {"name": "APIs Earn and Maintain Consumer Trust", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-earn-and-maintain-consumer-trust/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}]]]}
a.title: Deprecation (Lifecycle) — policy 2 strategies · 8 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Retirement (Lifecycle)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/lifecycle-retirement/", "text": "Require that retiring an API is a deliberate, documented step that only happens after a deprecation period, with the shutdown date, the reason, and the alternative all made clear to consumers. I want retirement to be the calm final chapter of a lifecycle we planned, not an abrupt disappearance that strands the people who relied on us. Confirm that traffic has drained, that migration paths exist, and that credentials, docs, and DNS are cleaned up so nothing lingers half-alive. Retiring APIs well is how we keep the catalog clean and prove that even the ending of an API is handled with respect.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Versioning", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/versioning/"}, {"name": "Deletion", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/deletion/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Gracefully Deprecated and Retired", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-gracefully-deprecated-and-retired/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Retirement (Lifecycle) — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Logging Is Standardized", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/logging-standardized/", "text": "Require that every API emit standardized, structured logs with consistent fields for request identity, timing, status, and correlation. I expect logs to follow a shared schema across services so they can be searched, joined, and reasoned about without decoding a different format for each team. Standardized logging is what turns an incident from a guessing game into a traceable timeline, and it is the foundation for both debugging and accountability. Free-form or missing logs leave operators blind, so I treat a consistent logging standard as a production requirement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Logging", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/logging/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable Across Operations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-across-operations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Logging Is Standardized — policy 1 strategies · 2 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Login for APIs", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/login/", "text": "Providing a way to login and gain access to an API, offering a simple human-readable URL to the login page, or ideally some sort of automated login process that allows access with as few clicks and steps as possible.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}]]]}
a.title: Login for APIs — policy 0 strategies · 2 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Maintainers", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/maintainers/", "text": "Require that every API names its maintainers, the real people or team accountable for its design, operation, and support, and records them where the contract lives. I care about this from the very first define stage because an API with no clear owner is an orphan waiting to happen, and orphaned APIs are how outages, security holes, and abandoned integrations get created. Naming maintainers gives consumers someone to reach, gives governance someone to hold accountable, and makes collaboration across teams possible instead of a guessing game. Ownership is the foundation everything else in the lifecycle is built on.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Domains", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/domains/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Development Is Collaborative Across Teams", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-development-is-collaborative-across-teams/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Collaboration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/collaboration/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Workspaces", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/workspaces/"}]]]}
a.title: Maintainers — policy 1 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "MCP Server Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/mcp-server-provided/", "text": "I require that an API of consequence exposes a Model Context Protocol server so that agents can discover its capabilities and invoke them through a standard, well-understood interface rather than a bespoke one we have to explain over and over. The MCP server should be a governed, documented artifact that maps cleanly to the underlying API, not a science project bolted on the side. I hold this position because MCP is quickly becoming the way agents connect to the tools they use, and providers who supply a clean server become reusable across a whole ecosystem while everyone else gets wrapped in someone else's brittle glue code. Every production API should treat its MCP server as part of the product.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Expose an MCP Server", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-expose-an-mcp-server/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json MCP Server Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-mcp-server-info/"}]]]}
a.title: MCP Server Provided — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Monetization Cost Attribution", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/monetization-cost-attribution/", "text": "I require that API usage and its costs can be attributed back to the team, application, or consumer that generated them, so the true cost of operating and consuming an API is visible rather than smeared across a shared bill nobody owns. Without attribution, an API looks free to the teams using it and expensive to the team running it, and that mismatch quietly distorts every decision about the API's future. I insist on this in production because a sustainable cost model depends on knowing who drives the cost, and that knowledge only exists if we design attribution in rather than reconstruct it from logs later. Every monetized API must attribute its costs to a clear owner.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Monetization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monetization/"}, {"name": "Analytics", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/analytics/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Have a Sustainable Cost Model", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-a-sustainable-cost-model/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}, {"name": "Sustainability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/sustainability/"}]]]}
a.title: Monetization Cost Attribution — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Monetization Metering", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/monetization-metering/", "text": "I require that every monetized API meters usage accurately and makes the units it counts explicit, so both the provider and the consumer agree on exactly what is being measured and billed. Metering is the foundation of any honest cost model, and if we cannot count consistently we cannot charge fairly or let a consumer predict their bill. I care about this because opaque or inconsistent metering erodes trust faster than almost anything else in an API relationship, and it makes analytics and forecasting impossible for everyone involved. Every API that charges for use must define and publish how it meters, and expose that usage so consumers can observe it themselves.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Monetization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monetization/"}, {"name": "Analytics", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/analytics/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Have a Sustainable Cost Model", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-a-sustainable-cost-model/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Sustainability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/sustainability/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}]]]}
a.title: Monetization Metering — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Monetization Plans Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/monetization-plans-defined/", "text": "I require that every API in production publishes its access plans as machine-readable definitions, so consumers can see the tiers, the limits, and the pricing without emailing a salesperson or guessing from a marketing page. A plan is a business contract, and it belongs in the API's metadata where it can be discovered, compared, and reasoned about alongside the technical interface. I insist on this because an API with hidden or undefined plans is impossible to adopt with confidence, and the ambiguity always favors the provider at the consumer's expense. Every monetized API must treat its plans as a published, governed artifact, not a PDF buried on a pricing page.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Monetization", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monetization/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Have a Sustainable Cost Model", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-a-sustainable-cost-model/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}, {"name": "Sustainability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/sustainability/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Plans Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-plans-info/"}]]]}
a.title: Monetization Plans Defined — policy 1 strategies · 3 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Observability Is Instrumented", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/observability-instrumented/", "text": "Every API must be instrumented for observability, exposing metrics, traces, and health signals that let operators understand its behavior in real time. I require that latency, error rates, and throughput be measurable per operation, and that traces carry across service boundaries. You cannot govern, scale, or trust what you cannot see, and observability is the difference between detecting a problem and being told about it by consumers. I hold instrumented observability as a baseline so that reliability is something we measure rather than something we hope for.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Monitoring", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monitoring/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable Across Operations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-across-operations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Observability Is Instrumented — policy 1 strategies · 2 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Open Source Tooling Preferred", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/open-source-tooling-preferred/", "text": "Require that an API operation prefers open source tooling and applies open licensing to its definitions, SDKs, and supporting tools wherever practical. Open source lets consumers understand, extend, and trust what they are building on, and it keeps an operation from being captive to a single vendor's roadmap. Choosing open tooling is both a practical efficiency and a statement about the kind of ecosystem you want to be part of.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Prefer Open Standards and Open Source", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-prefer-open-standards-and-open-source/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Openness", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/openness/"}, {"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Standardization", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/standardization/"}]]]}
a.title: Open Source Tooling Preferred — policy 1 strategies · 4 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Open Standards Adopted", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/open-standards-adopted/", "text": "Require that APIs are defined and delivered using open standards such as OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and JSON Schema rather than proprietary formats. Open specifications lower the cost of adoption, enable interoperability, and protect consumers from being locked into one vendor's way of doing things. Every proprietary shortcut becomes a tax paid by everyone downstream, so I treat open standards as the default rather than the exception.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Avoid Vendor Lock-In", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-avoid-vendor-lock-in/"}, {"name": "APIs Prefer Open Standards and Open Source", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-prefer-open-standards-and-open-source/"}, {"name": "APIs Serve the Public Interest", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-serve-the-public-interest/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Openness", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/openness/"}, {"name": "Standardization", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/standardization/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Portability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/portability/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}
a.title: Open Standards Adopted — policy 3 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "OpenAPI", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi/", "text": "A machine-readable OpenAPI using the most recent version of the API specification, describing the surface area of each API, which is then used to render the human-readable documentation, and other supporting elements.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Definitions", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/definitions/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs are Defined by Technical Contracts", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-defined-by-technical-contracts/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Apis Properties OpenAPI Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-apis-properties-openapi-info/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "HTTP Methods (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-http-methods/", "text": "Require that every operation in an OpenAPI definition uses the correct HTTP method for the action it performs, GET to read, POST to create, PUT and PATCH to update, DELETE to remove, and that we do not smuggle state changes into a GET or overload a single verb to do everything. I have debugged too many APIs where a POST quietly deleted data or a GET had side effects, and that ambiguity breaks caching, retries, and every consumer's mental model. When our methods mean what the web says they mean, tooling and developers can reason about our API without reading the source code. This is the most basic contract we make with the protocol, and it is worth getting right.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}
a.title: HTTP Methods (OpenAPI) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "HTTP Status Codes (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-http-status-codes/", "text": "Require that every operation documents the HTTP status codes it can actually return, using the standard families the way the web intends, 2xx for success, 3xx for redirection, 4xx for consumer mistakes, and 5xx for our own failures. I have wasted whole afternoons on APIs that answered every request with a 200 and buried the real outcome in the body, and that habit makes integrations brittle and error handling guesswork. When our status codes are honest and enumerated in the contract, consumers can build retry logic, alerting, and branching that just works. Status codes are a shared language, and I expect every API to speak it correctly.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Monitoring", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monitoring/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Operation ID Conventions (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-id-conventions/", "text": "Require that every operation in our OpenAPI definitions carries a unique, human-readable operationId that follows a consistent naming convention across the whole surface, something like getUser or listOrders rather than an autogenerated blob. I have generated SDKs and client code from specs with missing or clashing operation IDs, and the result is method names no developer would ever want to call. Because code generators, mock servers, and documentation tools all lean on the operationId, a clean and predictable convention pays off everywhere downstream. This is a small discipline at design time that saves everyone real friction later.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "2xx Response Examples (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-2xx-examples/", "text": "Require that every successful 2xx response in our OpenAPI definitions includes at least one realistic example, so a consumer can see exactly what a good answer looks like without making a live call. I have onboarded to too many APIs where the schema was technically complete but I still could not picture the actual payload, and examples are what close that gap. Good examples power interactive documentation, mock servers, and generated tests, and they set the expectation for what a healthy integration receives. I treat a missing success example as a documentation gap that we fix before the API ships.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "2xx Response Media Types (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-2xx-media-types/", "text": "Require that every 2xx response declares the media types it returns, spelling out application/json or whatever content it actually serves rather than leaving the content negotiation a mystery. I have integrated with APIs that promised JSON and quietly returned HTML on a good day, and that kind of surprise breaks parsers and erodes trust immediately. When the successful response media types are explicit in the contract, consumers can set the right Accept headers and deserialize with confidence, and our tooling can validate that we deliver what we promised. Content type is part of the contract, and I want it stated plainly for every success path.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "2xx Response Schema (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-2xx-schema/", "text": "Require that every 2xx response defines a schema for its body, describing the exact shape, properties, and types a consumer will receive on success rather than handing back an undocumented blob. I have written integrations against APIs whose success responses were a shrug, and every field became a discovery exercise in production. A concrete response schema lets consumers generate models, validate payloads, and trust the structure they are coding against, and it lets our own tests catch drift before it reaches anyone. If we cannot describe what success looks like, we do not really understand our own API yet.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "4xx Response Examples (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-4xx-examples/", "text": "Require that our 4xx client-error responses carry real examples, so a developer can see exactly what a validation failure, an unauthorized call, or a missing resource actually returns. I have spent far too long guessing at error payloads because the happy path was documented and the failure path was left blank, and that is where integrations really live or die. Concrete error examples let consumers build the branching and messaging that turn a frustrating dead end into a graceful recovery. I care as much about how our APIs fail as how they succeed, and examples are how we make the failure legible.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Documentation", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/documentation/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "4xx Response Media Types (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-4xx-media-types/", "text": "Require that every 4xx client-error response declares its media type, so consumers know whether an error comes back as application/json, application/problem+json, or something else entirely. I have hit APIs that returned tidy JSON on success and a wall of HTML on a 400, and code that tries to parse both ends up fragile and defensive for no good reason. When error responses use a declared, consistent media type, consumers can deserialize failures the same way they handle successes and react intelligently. Errors deserve the same content discipline as everything else, and I expect that stated in the contract.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "4xx Response Schema (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-4xx-schema/", "text": "Require that our 4xx client-error responses define a schema, ideally a consistent error object with a code, a message, and enough detail for a consumer to understand what went wrong and how to fix it. I have integrated with APIs whose errors were free-form strings that changed shape from one endpoint to the next, and building reliable handling on top of that is miserable. A defined error schema, applied uniformly across the surface, lets consumers parse failures programmatically and lets us evolve error messaging without breaking anyone. Standardized, well-described errors are one of the clearest signals of a mature API.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "5xx Response Media Types (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-5xx-media-types/", "text": "Require that every 5xx server-error response declares its media type, so that even when our own infrastructure fails, consumers still receive a predictable, parseable body instead of whatever a proxy or load balancer happened to emit. I have watched a 500 return raw HTML from some middlebox while the rest of the API spoke clean JSON, and that inconsistency shows up at the worst possible moment for the consumer. When our server errors use a declared media type, client error handling stays uniform across success and catastrophic failure alike. The failure case is exactly when consistency matters most, and I want it defined in the contract.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "5xx Response Schema (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-response-5xx-schema/", "text": "Require that our 5xx server-error responses define a schema, reusing the same standardized error object we use elsewhere so a consumer can handle our failures the same way they handle everything else. I have seen server errors leak stack traces and internal details in one case and return an empty body in the next, and neither helps the developer on the other end nor protects us. A defined 5xx schema lets us hand back a correlation id and a safe, useful message that a consumer can log, surface, and act on without scraping. Even when we break, we owe consumers a described, consistent response, and this is how we honor that.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Responses Must Be Meaningful and Consistent", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-responses-must-be-meaningful-and-consistent/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "OpenAPI Overlays Used", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-overlays-used/", "text": "Require that consistent, cross-cutting changes to OpenAPI definitions be applied through OpenAPI Overlays rather than by hand-editing each specification. I want shared conventions, added examples, governance annotations, and audience-specific variants expressed as overlays that layer cleanly over a source definition. This keeps the canonical spec authoritative while letting teams reuse a single set of adjustments across many APIs without drift. Copy-and-paste edits are how standards decay; overlays are how we keep definitions consistent and reusable, so I hold their use as a design-time expectation.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Provide Orchestration Workflows", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-provide-orchestration-workflows/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json Overlay Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-overlay-info/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Path Trailing Slashes (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-path-trailing-slashes/", "text": "Require that our OpenAPI paths follow one consistent rule about trailing slashes, and I strongly prefer no trailing slash so that /orders and /orders/ never become two subtly different things. I have chased 404s and duplicated cache entries that all traced back to a stray slash that some routers treat as significant and others silently redirect. Picking one convention and enforcing it across every path removes an entire category of consumer confusion and gateway misconfiguration. This is a tiny detail, but consistency in the small things is exactly what separates a polished API from a frustrating one.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Terms of Service", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/terms-of-service/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}]]]}
a.title: Path Trailing Slashes (OpenAPI) — policy 1 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Schema Constraints (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-schema-constraints/", "text": "Require that our schemas express real constraints on their properties, the minLength and maxLength, minimum and maximum, patterns, and formats that describe what valid data actually is rather than leaving every string and number wide open. I have seen unconstrained schemas let garbage flow straight into a database and turn into a support ticket weeks later. When the contract states the bounds up front, gateways and generated validators can reject bad input at the edge, and consumers know exactly what we will accept before they ever send it. Well-defined constraints are the difference between a schema that documents and a schema that actually protects the data.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Schema Property Enums (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-schema-property-enums/", "text": "Require that any property with a fixed set of allowed values declares those values as an enum in the schema, so status, type, and category fields cannot drift into a free-for-all of typos and invented strings. I have watched a single unconstrained status field accumulate a dozen near duplicate values across teams, and untangling that mess after the fact is painful. When the legal values live in the contract, consumers can code against them safely, tooling can validate them automatically, and everyone shares one vocabulary. Enums are a small act of design discipline that keeps our data clean and our meaning unambiguous.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Schema Property Required (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-schema-property-required/", "text": "Require that our schemas explicitly list which properties are required, so consumers know which fields they can always count on and which ones may be absent. I have written code that trusted a field to always be present, only to have it vanish on some records because the contract never actually said it was required. Marking required properties turns an implicit assumption into a stated guarantee that validators enforce and generated models respect. This is fundamental to well-defined, validated data, and leaving the required list empty by default is a habit I want us to break at design time.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Schema Required (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-schema-required/", "text": "Require that every request and response body in our OpenAPI definitions references a defined schema rather than accepting or returning free-form, untyped content. I have run into operations that declared a body but never described it, and a schema-less payload is just a promise to argue about the shape later. Anchoring each body to a named, reusable schema means our data is described in one place, validated everywhere, and safe to generate code and mocks against. If we are moving data in or out of an API, I expect a schema to govern it, because undefined data is undefended data.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "Data Should Be Well-Defined and Validated", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/data-should-be-well-defined-and-validated/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Servers (OpenAPI)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-servers/", "text": "Require that every OpenAPI definition declares its servers, the concrete base URLs where the API actually lives, ideally with an entry for each environment so production and sandbox are both discoverable from the contract. I have received specs with no servers block at all, forcing every consumer to hunt through docs or ask around just to make a first call. When the servers are stated in the definition, tooling can generate working clients, mock and gateway routing have a real target, and the API becomes something you can reach through the platform rather than a guessing game. The contract should tell you where the API is, not just what it does.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Made Available Through a Platform Gateway", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-made-available-through-a-platform-gateway/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Contracts", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/contracts/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Operations Are Agent-Legible", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-are-agent-legible/", "text": "I require that every operation in an OpenAPI carries a description rich enough that an agent can decide, from the definition alone, what the operation does, when to call it, and what it will get back. A terse summary that satisfies a human skimming the docs is not sufficient when the reader is a model reasoning about which call to make next. I insist on this at design time because agents do not have the benefit of a support channel or institutional knowledge, and a vague description quietly produces a wrong integration nobody notices until it fails in production. APIs should write operation descriptions as if the only reader is a capable machine that will take every word literally.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Legible to Automated Consumers", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-legible-to-automated-consumers/"}, {"name": "APIs Are Ready for AI Agents", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-ready-for-ai-agents/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "OpenAPI Operation Description Agent Sufficient Warn", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/openapi-operation-description-agent-sufficient-warn/"}]]]}
a.title: Operations Are Agent-Legible — policy 2 strategies · 5 experiences · 1 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Caching (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-caching/", "text": "Require that every read-heavy API sets explicit HTTP caching headers, so I want Cache-Control, ETag, and Last-Modified in play with sensible max-age and validation behavior spelled out in the contract. I lean on caching because the cheapest, fastest request is the one your origin never has to serve, and consumers who can safely reuse a response put far less load on your infrastructure. Left undefined, caching becomes accidental, and you end up with either stale data burning trust or no caching at all burning money. Decide it deliberately, document it, and enforce it at the gateway so the behavior is consistent across every endpoint.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Caching", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/caching/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Scale Efficiently Under Load", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-scale-efficiently-under-load/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}
a.title: Caching (Operations) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Error Handling (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-error-handling/", "text": "Require that every API returns standardized, informative errors, so I want a consistent error envelope, a correct HTTP status code, a machine-readable code, and a human-readable message on every failure path. I treat errors as part of the interface, not an afterthought, because the moment something goes wrong is exactly when a developer needs your API to be clear and honest with them. Vague, inconsistent, or leaky errors are where integrations die and support tickets are born. I like Problem Details for HTTP APIs as the baseline, never leak stack traces or internal details, and I enforce the shape at the gateway so it holds across every team and endpoint.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Errors Are Standardized and Informative", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-errors-are-standardized-and-informative/"}, {"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}
a.title: Error Handling (Operations) — policy 2 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Filtering & Sorting (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-filtering-sorting/", "text": "Require that collection endpoints offer consistent, documented filtering and sorting, so I want a shared convention for query parameters, allowed fields, operators, and sort order applied the same way across every list your API exposes. I care about this because letting consumers ask for exactly the data they need is how you keep payloads small, queries fast, and clients simple. When every endpoint invents its own filtering grammar, developers waste time relearning your API on each call and your backend gets hammered by clients over-fetching. Constrain filterable fields deliberately to protect your datastore, document the rules, and enforce them so the pattern is predictable everywhere.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}, {"name": "APIs Scale Efficiently Under Load", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-scale-efficiently-under-load/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Filtering & Sorting (Operations) — policy 2 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Health Checks (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-health-checks/", "text": "Require that every API exposes a standard health check endpoint, so I want a predictable path that reports liveness and readiness along with the status of critical dependencies. I insist on this because you cannot operate what you cannot see, and a machine-readable health signal is what lets load balancers, orchestrators, and monitoring systems make good decisions without guessing. When health checks are missing or bespoke, outages get noticed by your customers before they get noticed by you. I favor a common format like the health check response draft so tooling can consume it consistently, and I keep the endpoint honest about downstream failures rather than always returning a cheerful green.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}, {"name": "Monitoring", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monitoring/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable and Monitored", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-and-monitored/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}]]]}
a.title: Health Checks (Operations) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Logging (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-logging/", "text": "Require that every API produces structured, correlated logs for each request, so I want a consistent log schema, a correlation or trace identifier carried through, and clear rules about what gets captured and what never does. I care about logging because it is the record you fall back on when something breaks, when a consumer disputes what happened, or when you need to understand how your API is actually being used. Unstructured or missing logs turn every incident into an archaeology project. Just as important, I require that we never log secrets, tokens, or sensitive personal data, and that retention is deliberate, so our observability does not become its own liability.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}, {"name": "Logging", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/logging/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Provenance Is Maintained and Auditable", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-provenance-is-maintained-and-auditable/"}, {"name": "APIs Are Observable and Monitored", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-and-monitored/"}, {"name": "APIs Meet Regulatory and Compliance Requirements", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-meet-regulatory-and-compliance-requirements/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Provenance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/provenance/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Monitoring (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-monitoring/", "text": "Require that every API is actively monitored for availability, latency, error rates, and traffic, so I want the golden signals collected, dashboarded, and wired to alerts before an API ever reaches production. I hold this line because an API you are not watching is an API you are discovering the health of through angry customers, and that is the most expensive way to learn. Monitoring is what turns a two-hour outage into a two-minute one and gives you the data to make honest capacity and reliability decisions. I want thresholds and alerts defined as part of the contract, not bolted on later, so observability is a first-class requirement rather than a nice-to-have.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}, {"name": "Monitoring", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/monitoring/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable and Monitored", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-and-monitored/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}]]]}
a.title: Monitoring (Operations) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Pagination (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-pagination/", "text": "Require that every endpoint returning a collection paginates its results using a single, consistent strategy, so I want a documented approach, whether cursor or offset, with clear page-size limits and predictable navigation links or tokens. I am firm on this because an unbounded list is a loaded gun pointed at both your database and your consumers, and the day a collection grows large is the day an un-paginated endpoint takes something down. Consistency matters just as much as the mechanism itself, since developers should not have to relearn how to page through data on every resource. Cap the maximum page size, default it sensibly, and enforce the pattern at the gateway so it holds everywhere.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}, {"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Follow Consistent Design Patterns", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-follow-consistent-design-patterns/"}, {"name": "APIs Scale Efficiently Under Load", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-scale-efficiently-under-load/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}
a.title: Pagination (Operations) — policy 2 strategies · 9 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Rate Limiting (Operations)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/operations-rate-limiting/", "text": "Require that every API enforces rate limits and communicates them clearly, so I want defined quotas per consumer, standard headers that report remaining budget, and a proper 429 with a Retry-After when a limit is crossed. I treat rate limiting as basic self-defense, because it is what keeps one noisy or buggy client from degrading the experience for everyone else and what lets your platform scale predictably under load. Just as important, limits that are invisible are limits developers cannot design around, so I insist the contract tells consumers exactly what their budget is and how to back off gracefully. Enforce it at the gateway so the policy is uniform and hard to route around.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Management", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/management/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Made Available Through a Platform Gateway", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-made-available-through-a-platform-gateway/"}, {"name": "APIs Scale Efficiently Under Load", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-scale-efficiently-under-load/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Change", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/change/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Self-Service", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/self-service/"}, {"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Performance Budgets Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/performance-budgets/", "text": "Require that every API define performance budgets, setting explicit targets for latency, throughput, and error rates that it commits to holding. I expect these budgets to be measured continuously and treated as a contract the team defends, not an aspiration it mentions once. Performance budgets give consumers a dependable basis for their own architecture and give providers an early warning when a change degrades the experience. Without stated budgets, performance erodes quietly until it becomes an incident, so I hold defined budgets as a production requirement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Performance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Fast and Efficient", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-fast-and-efficient/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}]]]}
