a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Procurement Evaluation Checklist", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/procurement-evaluation-checklist/", "text": "Require that every API considered for adoption be run through a documented procurement evaluation checklist before a team commits to it. I want the same questions asked each time, covering security, licensing, reliability, support, pricing, and exit, so that adoption decisions rest on evidence rather than a demo and a good feeling. A shared checklist makes evaluations comparable across candidates and defensible to the people who sign off on the spend. Skipping this step is how organizations accumulate risky, redundant dependencies, so I hold a consistent evaluation checklist as a requirement at discovery time.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Evaluated Before Adoption", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-evaluated-before-adoption/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Procurement", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/procurement/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Reuse", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reuse/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Reuse Scoring Applied", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/reuse-scoring-applied/", "text": "Require that every API carry a reuse score that measures how widely and effectively it is being reused across teams and how much it duplicates existing capabilities. I want reuse assessed with a consistent, published method so we can reward APIs that serve many consumers and surface redundant efforts before they multiply. Reuse scoring turns a vague ideal into a governable signal that guides investment, retirement, and discovery decisions. An API portfolio that is never scored for reuse drifts toward sprawl and duplication, so I hold applied reuse scoring as a production-grade governance requirement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Evaluated Before Adoption", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-evaluated-before-adoption/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reuse", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reuse/"}, {"name": "Reusability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reusability/"}, {"name": "Procurement", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/procurement/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Abuse Prevention (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-abuse-prevention/", "text": "Require that every API is designed to resist abuse and misuse, so I want throttling, quotas, anomaly detection, bot and scraping defenses, and sensible request limits treated as part of the contract rather than something we react to after an incident. I push on this because a public API is a standing invitation, and not everyone who shows up has good intentions, so you have to assume some traffic will try to overwhelm, enumerate, or extract more than you intended to give. Prevention is dramatically cheaper than cleanup once your data has been scraped or your service has been knocked over. Bake these protections in at design time, tune them against real traffic, and enforce them at the gateway so abuse is expensive for the attacker and cheap for you to shrug off.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Protected from Abuse and Misuse", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-protected-from-abuse-and-misuse/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Scalability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/scalability/"}, {"name": "Performance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/performance/"}]]]}
a.title: Abuse Prevention (Security) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Authentication", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-authentication/", "text": "The details for how to authenticate with an API should always be part of the business and technical contracts for an API. Information on how to authenticate with an API should be readily available for developers and travel anywhere documentation for an API will be traveling.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Authentication", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/authentication/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Authentication Is Standardized", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-authentication-is-standardized/"}, {"name": "API Authorization Is Properly Defined and Enforced", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-authorization-is-properly-defined-and-enforced/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Onboarding", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/onboarding/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Authorization (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-authorization/", "text": "Require that every API defines and enforces authorization explicitly, so I want each operation to declare what scopes, roles, or permissions it demands and to check them on every request, not just at the front door. I separate this hard from authentication, because knowing who a caller is tells you nothing about what they are allowed to do, and broken object-level and function-level authorization are consistently among the most damaging API vulnerabilities out there. Default to deny, grant the least privilege that gets the job done, and make sure a user can never reach data or actions that belong to someone else. Define the authorization model in the contract and enforce it consistently so access control is deliberate rather than assumed.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Authorization Is Properly Defined and Enforced", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-authorization-is-properly-defined-and-enforced/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}]]]}
a.title: Authorization (Security) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "CORS (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-cors/", "text": "Require that every browser-facing API sets a deliberate, least-privilege CORS policy, so I want explicit allowed origins, methods, and headers rather than a lazy wildcard slapped on to make an error go away. I care about this because CORS is a security boundary, and a careless Access-Control-Allow-Origin of star, especially paired with credentials, quietly hands your API to any website that wants to ride a user's session. Name the origins you actually trust, scope the allowed methods and headers to what your clients really use, and treat any loosening of the policy as a decision that gets reviewed. Define it in the contract and enforce it at the gateway so browser access is intentional, not accidental.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Data Is Classified and Protected", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-data-is-classified-and-protected/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Access", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/access/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}]]]}
a.title: CORS (Security) — policy 1 strategies · 5 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Data Classification (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-data-classification/", "text": "Require that every API classifies the data it moves and applies protections that match that classification, so I want fields and payloads labeled as public, internal, confidential, or regulated, with encryption, masking, and access rules following from the label. I insist on this because you cannot protect what you have not named, and the difference between an ordinary endpoint and a compliance incident is usually whether anyone stopped to ask what kind of data was flowing through it. Classification is what lets you apply the right controls to PII, health, or financial data without over-locking everything else and grinding your platform to a halt. Do this work at design time, carry the labels into your contracts and tooling, and let them drive real enforcement rather than sitting in a spreadsheet.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Data Is Classified and Protected", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-data-is-classified-and-protected/"}, {"name": "APIs Meet Regulatory and Compliance Requirements", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-meet-regulatory-and-compliance-requirements/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}, {"name": "Alignment", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/alignment/"}]]]}
a.title: Data Classification (Security) — policy 2 strategies · 6 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Input Validation (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-input-validation/", "text": "Require that every API validates all incoming data against its schema before acting on it, so I want types, formats, lengths, ranges, and required fields checked at the edge and anything that does not conform rejected with a clear error. I am unbending on this because untrusted input is the root of a huge share of API breaches, from injection to overflow to malformed payloads that crash a handler, and the client cannot be trusted to send you clean data no matter how nicely you documented it. Validating against your OpenAPI schema turns your contract into a working defense rather than a suggestion. Reject early, reject clearly, and never let unvalidated data reach your business logic or datastore.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Testing", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/testing/"}, {"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Data Is Classified and Protected", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-data-is-classified-and-protected/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Quality", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/quality/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Transport (Security)", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/security-transport/", "text": "Require that every API is served exclusively over encrypted transport, so I want TLS enforced everywhere, plain HTTP either redirected or refused, weak protocols and ciphers disabled, and HSTS in place. I hold this as non-negotiable because anything traveling in the clear can be read or tampered with in transit, and there is simply no acceptable reason in this era to move credentials or data across an unencrypted connection. Strong transport security is also the foundation your consumers' trust is built on, since it is the visible promise that you take the confidentiality and integrity of their data seriously. Set a modern TLS baseline, keep it current as standards evolve, and verify it rather than assuming a certificate somewhere means the whole path is safe.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Governance", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/governance/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "API Data Is Classified and Protected", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/api-data-is-classified-and-protected/"}, {"name": "APIs Earn and Maintain Consumer Trust", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-earn-and-maintain-consumer-trust/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Security", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/security/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Compliance", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/compliance/"}, {"name": "Legal", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/legal/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Stability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/stability/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}]]]}
a.title: Transport (Security) — policy 2 strategies · 7 experiences · 0 rules

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "SLA Defined and Published", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/sla-defined-and-published/", "text": "I require that every production API defines a service level agreement and publishes it where consumers can find it, stating the availability, performance, and support commitments we are willing to stand behind. An SLA is a promise, and a promise that is not written down is not a promise at all, just a hope the consumer is left to guess about. I insist on this because integrators build real businesses on top of our APIs, and they deserve to know what reliability they can plan around and what recourse they have when we fall short. Every API that asks for production trust must define and publish its SLA as a governed part of its terms.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Terms of Service", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/terms-of-service/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Have a Sustainable Cost Model", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-have-a-sustainable-cost-model/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}, {"name": "Trust", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/trust/"}, {"name": "Sustainability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/sustainability/"}, {"name": "Money", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/money/"}, {"name": "Business", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/business/"}]], ["Rules", [{"name": "APIs.json SLA Info", "url": "https://rules.apievangelist.com/store/apis-json-sla-info/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Support Channels Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/support-channels-defined/", "text": "Require that every API publish clear support channels so consumers know exactly how to get help and what to expect when they ask. I want the path to a human, an issue tracker, or a community forum documented alongside the API, with the scope and hours of each channel made explicit. Support is part of the contract; an API without a way to raise problems leaves consumers stranded the moment something breaks. Naming and standing behind support channels signals that a provider intends to be a dependable partner, which is why I hold it as a requirement.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Support", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/support/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Observable Across Operations", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-observable-across-operations/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Developer Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/developer-experience/"}, {"name": "Communication", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/communication/"}, {"name": "Observability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/observability/"}, {"name": "Reliability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/reliability/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Tool Definitions Provided", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/tool-definitions-provided/", "text": "I require that APIs publish explicit tool definitions that describe each callable capability as a discrete tool an agent can select, with clear names, descriptions, and typed inputs and outputs. These definitions should be authored deliberately during design, not reverse-engineered from an endpoint list after the fact, because the quality of the description is what determines whether an agent picks the right tool for the job. I push for this at design time because an operation that is legible to a human is not automatically legible to a machine, and the difference between the two is a few careful sentences per tool. Every API meant for automated consumers must treat its tool definitions as a contract, versioned and reviewed like any other interface.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Are Legible to Automated Consumers", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-are-legible-to-automated-consumers/"}, {"name": "APIs Expose an MCP Server", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-expose-an-mcp-server/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Agent Experience", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/agent-experience/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Discovery", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/discovery/"}, {"name": "Consistency", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/consistency/"}, {"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}]]]}

a.data-info: {"kind": "Policy", "name": "Webhook Contracts Defined", "url": "https://policies.apievangelist.com/store/webhook-contracts-defined/", "text": "I require that every webhook an API sends is described by a real contract that specifies its trigger, its payload, its headers, and its delivery and retry behavior, so integrators can build against it with confidence instead of reverse-engineering it from a sample they caught in production. Webhooks are APIs that run in reverse, and they deserve the same definition, versioning, and governance we give the request-response surface. I hold this at design time because an undocumented webhook is a silent dependency that breaks integrations the moment its shape changes, usually without warning. Every API that pushes events must define its webhook catalog as a first-class, discoverable contract.", "groups": [["Lifecycle", [{"name": "Design", "url": "https://lifecycle.apievangelist.com/store/design/"}]], ["Strategies", [{"name": "APIs Use the Right Protocol for the Job", "url": "https://strategies.apievangelist.com/store/apis-use-the-right-protocol-for-the-job/"}]], ["Experiences", [{"name": "Integration", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/integration/"}, {"name": "Automation", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/automation/"}, {"name": "Interoperability", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/interoperability/"}, {"name": "Simplicity", "url": "https://experiences.apievangelist.com/store/simplicity/"}]]]}
